name: PAN-OS Anonymizer or Unusual Tunnel Application
description: Detects allowed traffic using a Palo Alto application identifier for DNS over HTTPS, QUIC-base, or WebDAV when Palo Alto assigns the application a high risk level. This is a vendor classification and does not by itself prove anonymisation abuse, malware, or a tunnel being used for an attack.
note:
## What this alert shows

An internal system made an allowed connection that Palo Alto identified as DNS over HTTPS, QUIC-base, or WebDAV with application risk level 4 or 5. These applications can be legitimate, so the alert requires context.

## What to check

Review the source and destination, application name, user if available, time, firewall action, security rule, and destination reputation. Confirm whether the application and destination are approved for the system and user. Look for repeated connections, unusual destinations, related DNS or threat alerts, and activity outside normal business use.

## Safe response

Preserve the relevant logs and confirm the business purpose with the system owner. Escalate repeated or unexplained activity to the SOC for review. Do not automatically block traffic, isolate a system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
author: SecurityOnion
query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"TRAFFIC" and panw.panos.action:allow and event.action:flow_started and panw.panos.application.tunneled:(dns-over-https or quic-base or webdav) and panw.panos.application.risk_level:(4 or 5)

name: PAN-OS High-Risk URL-Filtering Alert
description: Detects a PAN-OS URL-filtering event classified as high risk. The classification indicates that the web request deserves review; it does not by itself prove that the user visited a malicious site, downloaded malware, or was compromised.
note:
## What this alert shows

Palo Alto classified a URL or web request as high risk. The alert may represent a blocked or allowed request, and the result must be checked rather than assumed.

## What to check

Review the full URL or domain, source system, user if available, time, URL category, threat name, firewall action, security rule, and whether the request was allowed, blocked, or redirected. Check for repeated visits, downloads, related DNS or endpoint alerts, and whether the activity has a legitimate business purpose.

## Safe response

Preserve the relevant web, DNS, and endpoint evidence and confirm the activity with the user or system owner. Escalate unexplained or corroborated activity to the SOC. Do not automatically block the domain, isolate the system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
author: SecurityOnion
query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"THREAT" and event.kind:alert and event.action:url_filtering and panw.panos.action:alert and panw.panos.application.risk_level:(4 or 5) and not panw.panos.url_category_list:"low-risk"

name: PAN-OS DNS Malware or New Domain Threat
description: Detects a PAN-OS DNS threat event classified as dns-malware or dns-new-domain. This classification is a warning for investigation and is not proof that the domain is malicious or that the system is compromised.
note:
## What this alert shows

Palo Alto classified DNS activity as possible malware-related or as involving a newly observed domain. The classification may be useful, but it can be wrong or benign and does not prove a successful attack.

## What to check

Review the full domain, source system, time, destination or resolver, threat name, severity, firewall action, and whether the request was blocked or allowed. Check how often the domain was requested, whether other systems contacted it, and whether the source has endpoint, process, authentication, or other threat evidence. Confirm whether the domain is approved.

## Safe response

Preserve the DNS and related logs and ask the system owner to confirm the activity. Escalate unknown, repeated, allowed, or corroborated activity to the SOC. Do not automatically block the domain, isolate the system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
author: SOC Manager
false_positives: Legitimate newly observed domains may match dns-new-domain; triage before suppression.
query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"THREAT" and panw.panos.threat_category:("dns-malware" or "dns-new-domain") and event.action:"spyware_detected"

name: PAN-OS Security Threat Alert (Non-URL)
description: Detects a PAN-OS non-URL threat event classified as spyware or exploit activity while excluding URL-filtering events. The alert identifies a security event for review; it does not by itself prove that exploitation succeeded or that the destination system was compromised.
note:
## What this alert shows

Palo Alto recorded a non-URL threat event, such as a possible exploit or spyware detection. The firewall action and surrounding events are needed to understand what happened.

## What to check

Review the threat name, category, severity, source and destination, application, destination port, time, security rule, and firewall action. Confirm whether the traffic was allowed, alerted, blocked, or dropped. Check the destination host for authentication, endpoint, application, and related threat evidence, and look for repeated events from the same source.

## Safe response

Preserve the alert and related logs and notify the destination system owner. Escalate promptly when the event was allowed, repeated, critical, or supported by other evidence. Do not automatically block traffic, isolate a system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
author: SecurityOnion
query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"THREAT" and event.kind:alert and panw.panos.action:alert and event.action:(spyware_detected or exploit_detected)

name: Palo Alto Device High Event
description: Detects a Palo Alto event classified as High severity. This is a vendor severity classification that requires prompt review, but it does not by itself prove a successful attack or compromise.
note:
## What this alert shows

Palo Alto marked an event as High severity. The severity is a warning about potential importance, not a complete assessment of impact.

## What to check

Review the event type, threat or application name, source, destination, port, time, firewall action, security rule, and whether the traffic was allowed or blocked. Check related alerts and source events, then confirm with the owner of the affected system whether the activity was expected.

## Safe response

Preserve the relevant evidence and escalate promptly to the SOC or system owner when the event is unexplained, allowed, repeated, or supported by other evidence. Do not automatically block traffic, isolate a system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on severity alone.
query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"THREAT" and event.kind:alert and event.severity:2

name: Palo Alto Device Low Event
description: Detects a Palo Alto event classified as Low severity. This is a vendor classification that may be informational or low risk, but the event should still be reviewed in context.
note:
## What this alert shows

Palo Alto marked an event as Low severity. Low severity does not mean that the event can always be ignored; it may provide useful context or become more important when combined with other activity.

## What to check

Review the event type, threat or application name, source, destination, port, time, firewall action, security rule, and whether related higher-severity alerts exist. Check whether the activity is expected and whether it repeats or involves the same system or source.

## Safe response

Preserve relevant logs and ask the system owner to confirm unexplained activity. Escalate repeated activity or activity supported by other evidence to the SOC. Do not automatically block traffic, isolate a system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"THREAT" and event.kind:alert and event.severity:4

name: Palo Alto Device Medium Event
description: Detects a Palo Alto event classified as Medium severity. This is a vendor classification that may indicate suspicious or policy-related activity and requires review in context; it does not by itself prove compromise.
note:
## What this alert shows

Palo Alto marked an event as Medium severity. The classification indicates that the event may need attention, but it is not a complete determination of risk or impact.

## What to check

Review the event type, threat or application name, source, destination, port, time, firewall action, security rule, and whether the traffic was allowed or blocked. Look for repeated activity, related higher-severity alerts, authentication events, and other evidence affecting the same system. Confirm whether the activity was expected with the system owner.

## Safe response

Preserve relevant logs and escalate unexplained, repeated, allowed, or corroborated activity to the SOC. Do not automatically block traffic, isolate a system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"THREAT" and event.kind:alert and event.severity:3

name: Possible FIN7 DGA Command and Control Behavior
description: Detects a domain name that matches a pattern sometimes associated with DGA-like activity. This does not prove FIN7 activity, malware, command-and-control communication, or compromise.
note:
## What this alert shows

A domain in a network event matched a pattern that can occur in algorithmically generated or otherwise suspicious-looking domain names. The pattern is only a warning and does not identify a threat group or prove malicious activity.

## What to check

Review the full domain, source system, time, destination address, DNS or connection frequency, firewall action, and whether the domain is approved. Check the source host for endpoint alerts, unusual processes, repeated lookups, and other suspicious connections. Compare the activity with normal use for that system.

## Safe response

Preserve the domain and related network or endpoint evidence and confirm the activity with the system owner. Escalate unknown, repeated, or corroborated activity to the SOC. Do not automatically block the domain, isolate the system, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone.
author: Elastic
false_positives: This rule could identify benign domains that are formatted similarly to FIN7's command and control algorithm. Alerts should be investigated by an analyst to assess the validity of the individual observations.
query: (event.dataset: (network_traffic.tls OR network_traffic.http) OR (event.category: (network OR network_traffic) AND type: (tls OR http) AND network.transport: tcp)) AND destination.domain:/[a-zA-Z]{4,5}\\.(pw|us|club|info|site|top)/ AND NOT destination.domain:zoom.us
